page_header.title: The HiFive English Story
page_header.subtitle: Here's an honest look at what our founder, 우종범, has wrestled with over 12 years of running a video English program — and what HiFive English is building today.

ceo_letter.author_label: A letter from our founder, 우종범
ceo_letter.author_sub: HiFive English · 12 years in video English education
paragraphs_1: Hello, I'm 우종범, founder of HiFive English.
As of 2026, it's been 12 years since I started this video English education business.
In that time, I've met countless students, parents, and teachers who worked alongside me. Through it all, one question has stayed with me longer than any other.
ceo_letter.pull_quote: "How do we make sure a student can actually use the English they've learned?"
paragraphs_2: Teaching English itself isn't the hard part. The hard part is getting a student to actually open their mouth and use it.

I've never been comfortable sticking with one approach for too long. I know it would be easier to keep a lesson format simply because it worked well last year. But doing that means standing still. So every year — sometimes every month — I ask myself the same questions again.
questions: Can this lesson be better than it is right now?
Is there a way to raise the quality of this teacher's classes?
Can we get the student to speak even a little more English in this lesson?
Is there a way for parents to understand their child's lessons more clearly than they do now?
paragraphs_3: The past 12 years have been a process of searching for answers to these questions, and HiFive English is the result of continually reshaping itself along the way.

I feel much the same way about pricing. A higher price doesn't always mean a better class, and chasing the lowest price shouldn't be the goal either. Cutting costs that have nothing to do with the quality of the lesson itself, and putting what's saved back into the actual teaching — that's what I consider a fair price.
HiFive English won't stay exactly as it is today. It will keep changing.

trust_section.title: We've grown through real stories, not advertising
paragraphs: Rather than spending heavily on advertising, HiFive English has grown mainly through the words of parents and students who have already taken our classes.

It wasn't a deliberate decision to avoid advertising. It's simply that, when it comes to education, nothing is more accurate than the words of someone who has actually taken the class. Ad copy can always be written to sound good, but what a child says right after a lesson, or what a parent writes in a review months later, can't be faked.
That's why HiFive English spends its time making each lesson better for the students we already have, rather than chasing new ones.

philosophy_section.title: Why "listening a lot" isn't enough
paragraphs: Students learning English in an EFL environment — where there's little occasion to use English in daily life — face a particular challenge. They spend plenty of time studying English, but nowhere near enough time actually using it.

Even students who know plenty of vocabulary and grammar often freeze up in front of a native speaker — not because their ability is lacking, but because they simply haven't had enough real experience putting that vocabulary and grammar to use.

This is where HiFive English's lessons begin. We don't stop at listening and understanding. Within each lesson, the student thinks through the content and puts it into their own words, the teacher corrects it on the spot, and the student says it again using the corrected expression — and this cycle repeats.
closing_paragraphs: When this cycle repeats several times within a single lesson, an expression finally shifts from something the student merely 'knows' to something they can actually 'use.'

That's why HiFive English teachers don't focus on simply finishing a textbook on schedule. They spend more time asking questions suited to each student's level and goals, keeping the conversation going, correcting sentences, and having students practice the same expression again and again in different situations.

parent_faq.title: What you're curious about, even without watching every lesson

items.q: Is my child actually speaking much English in class?
items.a: It's hard to know the answer for certain unless you sit in on the lesson yourself. That's why HiFive English treats a student's 'share of speaking time' as a key standard, starting from teacher training. We design lessons so that students speak for longer than teachers explain, and we factor this directly into teacher evaluations.

items.q: Is the teacher tailoring the lesson to my child specifically?
items.a: Even students of the same age and level are comfortable with different topics and struggle with different things. This is exactly why we make dedicated-teacher assignment a core principle. Instead of meeting a new student every time, a teacher keeps working with the same student, learning their habits and weak points and adjusting the lessons accordingly.

items.q: Does the teacher know where my child is falling short?
items.a: In the learning report left after every lesson, teachers record specific details — the expressions the student struggled with that day, and the grammar or pronunciation mistakes they made most often. The goal isn't a generic overall comment, but a genuinely useful record the teacher can refer back to in the next lesson.

items.q: What actually improves if my child takes lessons consistently?
items.a: We can't promise dramatic change in a short time. But as a student builds up experience actually using an expression, getting corrected on the spot, and using that same expression again in a different situation, they'll have more and more moments where English that once lived only in their head comes out naturally. You can track that progress through the monthly level test.

items.q: Can I understand how my child is progressing without watching every lesson myself?
items.a: Right now, the learning report provided after each lesson gives you a reasonable picture. But we're working on taking this a step further — see the 'Feedback System' section below for details.

feedback_system.title: What we're building now — more detailed lesson feedback
feedback_system.intro: Over 12 years of talking with parents, I've kept noticing the same thing: a one-line comment like "Great class today" just isn't enough for a parent to really understand their child's lesson.
feedback_system.body: That's why, aiming for a late-2026 launch, we're building a system that analyzes the full flow of a lesson from start to finish and delivers much more detailed feedback. It's not finished yet, but here's what we're aiming to include.
items: How much the student actually spoke during the lesson
Level of engagement in the lesson
Pronunciation or phrasing that could use improvement
What the student did well in this lesson
What to work on in the next lesson
feedback_system.closing: Our goal is to let parents know exactly what their child did, what they learned, and what they still need to practice today — without needing to sit beside them during the lesson. We're continuing to refine this system now, and it will keep getting better going forward.
